tagline: First spacecraft to observe the Sun's poles from above + below the ecliptic — Jupiter gravity assist 1992
description: Joint ESA + NASA solar / heliospheric mission, built by Dornier with US scientific contribution. Launched 1990-10-06 from STS-41 Discovery on a high-energy trajectory direct to Jupiter — the only way to fling a spacecraft out of the ecliptic plane without prohibitive delta-v. Jupiter flyby 1992-02-08 deflected the spacecraft into an 80°-inclination heliocentric orbit (1.3 × 5.4 AU, 6.2-year period) — the first and still only spacecraft to fly over the Sun's poles. Three complete polar orbits gave us the heliospheric current sheet 3D structure, the faster polar / slower equatorial solar wind, and the only multi-decade record of polar coronal hole behaviour over a complete solar cycle. Mission ended 2009.
best_known_for: Only spacecraft to fly over the Sun's poles — joint ESA / NASA, 1990-2009
